alternatives.ComputeShader: CPU calculation, a [BurstCompile] job (multithreaded on Web from Unity 6.4), or a Pixel Shader
alternatives.MultiThreadedRendering: Single-threaded rendering -- this entry covers RENDERING only. Unity 6.4 does run [BurstCompile] jobs on background workers for Web builds, so CPU work can be multithreaded by moving it into a Burst job; non-Burst jobs stay on the main thread.

disallowedAPIs: System.Threading.Thread (general-purpose OS threads are unavailable; use a [BurstCompile] job instead -- Unity 6.4 runs Burst jobs on background workers for Web)

graphicsApi.notes: WebGL does not support compute shaders, so the URP GPU Resident Drawer and other compute-shader-based render features are unavailable regardless of rendering path. Unity's WebGPU backend is an option for compute-class features but has a smaller browser support matrix than WebGL 2.0; Unity 6.4 adds PSO tracing and warming for WebGPU. Verify current maturity against the target Unity version rather than assuming a specific release's status.

unity64Notes.threading: Multithreaded RENDERING is still unavailable on Web, and general-purpose threads are still unsupported -- but Unity 6.4 enables multithreading for [BurstCompile] jobs on Web builds, which run on background workers. Non-Burst jobs stay on the main thread. Do not state that Web has no multithreading at all; state which kind.
unity64Notes.microphone: Unity 6.4 adds Microphone API support on Web.
unity64Notes.webgpu: Unity 6.4 adds PSO (pipeline state object) tracing and warming for the WebGPU backend.
